etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English plentiful, plentyfull, plentefull, equivalent to plenty +‎ -ful.

definitions.definition: Existing in large number or ample amount.

quote.citation: 1627 (indicated as 1626), Francis [Bacon], “(please specify the page, or |century=I to X)”, in Sylua Syluarum: Or A Naturall Historie. In Ten Centuries. […], London:  […]  William Rawley […]; [p]rinted by J[ohn] H[aviland] for William Lee […], →OCLC:
quote.text: If it be a long winter, it is commonly a more plentiful year.

quote.citation: 1625, Francis [Bacon], “Of Expense”, in The Essayes […], 3rd edition, London:  […]  Iohn Haviland for Hanna Barret, →OCLC:
quote.text: He that is plentiful in expenses will hardly be preserved from decay.
